items.a: Kenya Shipyards Limited was established by the Kenyan Government. The National Treasury has 100% shareholding.
The National Security Council approved establishment on 14 August 2020. The company was incorporated on 29 September 2020.

items.q: Which materials are used in shipbuilding?
items.a: Marine-grade steel is the bulk material. Hulls may also use aluminium, fibreglass, wood, or other materials depending on the vessel. Structural steel must satisfy classification societies.

items.q: How many ships has Kenya Shipyards built?
items.a: After 15 months of work, including shifts, KSL built a 100 metre wagon ferry floated on 2 August 2022 at Kisumu Shipyard.

items.q: How do suppliers register for KSL tenders?
items.a: Follow tender notices published by Kenya Shipyards Limited and the Government of Kenya procurement portals. Prepare company registration, tax compliance, and relevant maritime or engineering credentials.

items.q: Can MDAs order vessels through KSL?
items.a: Executive direction encourages ministries, departments, and agencies to source maritime products and services from KSL where applicable. Contact commercial services for specifications and lead times.

items.q: What services are available at Mombasa and Kisumu?
items.a: Both yards support new build, refit, repair, dry docking, GRP craft, and shore-side civil works. Mombasa focuses on coastal and naval workloads; Kisumu serves Lake Victoria and inland fleets.

items.q: How do I request a quote for a new vessel?
items.a: Contact KSL through the enquiry form on the Contact page or email publicaffairs@kenyashipyards.co.ke with vessel type, intended use, and delivery timeline.

items.q: How do I lodge a complaint?
items.a: Use the Customer Complaint Form available on the Downloads page and submit it per the instructions in the Citizen Service Delivery Charter.

items.q: What service standards does KSL commit to?
items.a: The Citizen Service Delivery Charter sets out response times, courtesy standards, and escalation paths. English and Kiswahili versions are published on Downloads.

items.q: Can the public visit Mombasa or Kisumu shipyards?
items.a: Yards are secure defence and industrial sites. Visits require prior coordination with KSL public affairs or the relevant host agency. Do not enter operational areas without escort.
Head office: Herufi House, Treasury Buildings, Nairobi. Shipyards: Mtongwe (Mombasa) and Marine Drive, Kisumu.
Vacancies are advertised on the Careers page when open. You may also send a general application to careers@kenyashipyards.co.ke for future consideration.

items.q: What safety regulations do shipbuilders need to follow?
items.a: KSL applies work safety and quality policies and Occupational Safety, Health and Environment regulations, together with classification society rules.
